review_notes: The file is one theorem. Its proof is a manual rw chain, so I checked the simp status of every lemma it rewrites with. Frobenius `_mk`, `coe_frobeniusPushforwardGeomLevelDegZero` and `coe_degZeroSMulHom` are already @[simp]. `Finsupp.mapDomain.addMonoidHom_apply` and `Finsupp.mapDomain_comp` come from Mathlib, and I did not inspect them. `divisor_smul_def` is deliberately not simp, because the simp lemma `smul_single` covers the single case and a simp `divisor_smul_def` would compete with it. The one clear gap is `SemilinearAut.pic0_smul_mk` (and, less strongly, `galois_smul_pic0_def`). I did not run Lean, so I make no claim about how the simplifier would behave on the proposed attribute. There is some uncertainty about whether tagging `pic0_smul_mk` @[simp] would change existing `simp` call sites elsewhere in the repository. I did not audit those.

findings.declaration: solution (uses SemilinearAut.pic0_smul_mk / galois_smul_pic0_def, which are not simp)
findings.problem: The `_mk` computation rule for the semilinear-automorphism action on Pic0, `SemilinearAut.pic0_smul_mk : g • Pic0.mk D = Pic0.mk (degZeroSMulHom g D)`, is not tagged @[simp]. Its sibling rules are simp: `coe_degZeroSMulHom` and `frobeniusPushforwardGeomLevelPic0OfIsCurveOver_mk`. The target therefore has to list the lemmas in a manual `rw` chain, and the same chain recurs across many solution files. In the same chain, `galois_smul_pic0_def` (`σ • x = arithmeticGalois F₀ σ • x`) is also only available by name. `Pic0.smul_mk` for the field-automorphism action in Def_AlgebraicCurve_DivisorClassGroup.lean has the same gap. The result is a split interface: simp can push `coe_degZeroSMulHom` and the Frobenius `_mk` lemma through `mk` terms, but cannot rewrite the action on `Pic0.mk` itself.
findings.proposed_change: Mark `SemilinearAut.pic0_smul_mk` (and `Pic0.smul_mk`) @[simp]. The rule is a reduction of `g • mk D` to `mk (degZeroSMulHom g D)`, and `coe_degZeroSMulHom` then continues the rewrite to `g • ↑D`. Both rules are rfl-lemmas, and I see no reverse rule or other competing rule on `g • mk D`. Consider also making `galois_smul_pic0_def` simp, or adding a simp lemma `σ • Pic0.mk D = Pic0.mk (degZeroSMulHom (arithmeticGalois F₀ σ) D)`. Then the head of this proof can be `simp only [...]`, or `simp` after `obtain ⟨D, rfl⟩`.
findings.benefit: Proofs about Galois action on Pic0 classes would be shorter and no longer need the exact lemma names in the right order. `simp` would reach the same normal form (`mk` of a divisor-level expression) that the existing simp lemmas `coe_degZeroSMulHom` and `..._mk` already assume. This pays off at the many call sites that currently spell out `rw [pic0_smul_mk, ...]`.

evidence.excerpt:
theorem pic0_smul_mk (g : SemilinearAut K F) (D : Divisor.degZero (K := K) (F := F)) :
    g • (Pic0.mk D) = Pic0.mk (degZeroSMulHom g D) := rfl

@[simp]
theorem coe_degZeroSMulHom (g : SemilinearAut K F) (D : Divisor.degZero (K := K) (F := F)) :
    (degZeroSMulHom g D : Divisor K F) = g • (D : Divisor K F) := rfl

theorem galois_smul_pic0_def (σ : L ≃ₐ[ℚ] L) (x : Pic0 L (laurentBaseChange L F₀)) :
    σ • x = arithmeticGalois F₀ σ • x :=
  rfl

· rw [pic0_smul_mk]
    exact congrArg Pic0.mk (Subtype.ext (by rw [coe_degZeroSMulHom]; rfl))
